question: Monochrome: is intentional rasterisation acceptable, or is a structure-preserving implementation required?
recommendation: Keep rasterisation (candidate A) for the M5 MVP only as an explicit INTENTIONAL_FLATTENING operation whose PLAN names every loss and requires confirmation, inside the Raster Budget; take candidate C (structure-preserving, fail-closed) forward as a separate spike measured on real drawings before it is offered.

question: Optimize — meaning: what does 「最適化」 promise (O1 flatten / O2 lossless / O3 preservation levels), and may O1 keep that name?
recommendation: O1 must not keep the name: measured, it removes all text and structure and makes vector drawings 11-153x larger at its default and up to 463x. O2 (lossless, never larger) is the floor 「最適化」 can promise today; whether it also means O3 depends on H2b.

question: Optimize — lossy contract for O3: target-DPI semantics, JPEG quality, whether lossy recompression is acceptable at all, raster linework / scanned-text quality, and skip-versus-recompress.
recommendation: Measured on a 300 dpi one-pixel linework scan: resampling to 150 dpi keeps only ~22-26% of the line ink whether lossless or JPEG; JPEG q0.8 at the scan's own resolution keeps 100% at x0.33. Recommended if adopted: never resample below the source resolution without an explicit per-run choice; JPEG only when smaller; quality >= 0.8; everything else skipped and reported.

question: Margin: which source structure must survive?
recommendation: Adopt the in-place transform with its exact contract: text, OCR, vectors, raster bytes, annotations (moved), links and their destinations (XYZ/Fit*/FitR, named, outlines — moved with their target page), form widgets and values (with /DA and border scaled), XFA, metadata, /Rotate and CropBox all survive; refused before any change: q/Q underflow, unknown annotation types, annotations not wholly inside the visible page, destinations of unknown type or into no page of the document, structure destinations, GoToE.

question: Batch failure: B1 fail whole, B2 explicit partial with a manifest, or B3 independent per-file jobs (one download per file, as each finishes)?
recommendation: B2 — one archive after the last file, the successes plus a manifest naming every file's PLAN, FileResult and reason, also on screen. Today's partial ZIP carries no record of the failure.

question: Searchable text / OCR: may an intentionally flattening operation remove it, and on what confirmation?
recommendation: Only with an explicit per-run confirmation that names the loss; never as a default and never silently.

question: Annotations and forms: preserve, refuse, or explicitly flatten — per operation?
recommendation: Structure-preserving operations preserve and transform them within the stated contract or refuse by name; flattening operations list them among the confirmed losses.

question: Signatures and XFA: given the common SourceFacts (readable, encrypted, pages, AcroForm, XFA, signature fields, form-inspection state), which policy decides — 'annotator-equivalent' (XFA always refused), 'refuse-if-dropped' (refuse only operations that drop XFA), or 'confirm-if-dropped' (a flattening may drop it on confirmation) — and does it cover the hardened lanes?
recommendation: Signed documents: refuse for every operation, the hardened lanes included — every candidate re-serialises, so the signature cannot survive. XFA: 'refuse-if-dropped' — measured, Layer, both hardened lanes and every structure-preserving candidate keep XFA through a re-save; only the operations that rebuild a document drop it.

question: Memory for the flattening operations: default and explicit override?
recommendation: MAX_OPERATION_MEMORY 512 MiB by default with explicit 1 GiB and 2 GiB, never raised automatically; MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES 256 MiB; checked by the Raster Budget model (conservative per-page, per-file and batch terms, JPEG bounded at 1.0 B/px from a measured worst case). Consequence at the default: A4 at 300 dpi Monochrome up to 30 pages; A1 at 300 dpi Monochrome needs 1 GiB; a batch up to 49 one-page A4 files at 150 dpi Optimize.

question: Raster resolution: which DPI are offered, and how is an impossible one refused without a silent downgrade?
recommendation: MAX_RASTER_PIXELS 134,217,728 (128 Mi px) as the portable policy ceiling — below the 139-279 Mpx boundary measured on one machine, not that boundary itself — plus a runtime canvas-allocation probe before each page that refuses if it fails. The UI keeps its options; the preflight refuses with the numbers (A0 at 300 dpi, A1 and A0 at 600 dpi) and never lowers the DPI.

question: Cancellation: atomic output and ownership — does a settings change, file change or navigation supersede a run?
recommendation: Yes: the F1-B/M4 owner token, captured at start and re-read at every file boundary and immediately before each publish; unmount, a settings change and a file-list change supersede. Under B3 a file's own change supersedes that file only.

question: Common Processor orchestration: one PLAN/RESULT engine, or per-tool engines?
recommendation: One orchestration (SourceFacts, the H7 policy, the Raster Budget, ownership, the batch policy, publish) with per-operation planners and runners; the hardened lanes enter it unchanged behind the common facts step.

question: Metadata: which operations may change the Info dictionary and XMP, and must a flattening operation carry them into the new document?
recommendation: No operation changes metadata silently: preserve Info/XMP (load with updateMetadata: false; copy them into rebuilt documents) unless the Human Gate names a change.

question: Layer extent: does the overlay cover the visible page (CropBox ∩ MediaBox) or the MediaBox from (0,0)?
recommendation: The visible page, in the page's own coordinates; today it misses 61% of the ink when the MediaBox does not start at the origin.

question: Layer stacking: does the overlay sit below annotations (as today) or above them?
recommendation: Measured: today the overlay is below every annotation (content stream), with no rewriting. 'Above' is possible without flattening only as one more annotation painted last — it then is an annotation itself (selectable, deletable, printed by its /F flag). Recommend below, stated in the UI; 'above' only if the Human Gate accepts an overlay annotation.
